The "Could not find: libnccl-net.so" and "NCCL INFO P2P is disabled" do not appear to be fatal, and I would guess are not directly related to the failure.
Can you try with the latest jax and jaxlib version 0.4.31?
It fails with the same errors.

It looks like your network is not configured properly based on this warning:
`misc/ibvwrap.cc:206 NCCL WARN Call to ibv_modify_qp failed with error Invalid argument errno 22`
Your cross-node comm interface is using RoCE:
`host1:20632:21039 [3] NCCL INFO NET/IB : Using [0]irdma0:1/RoCE [RO]; `

This usually happens when the NIC is not configured properly to use RoCE.
Here is some debugging info provided by NCCL:
https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html#rdma-over-converged-ethernet-roce

Can you also use this perftest(https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest) tool to see if your network is RoCE enabled?
Thanks, I'll follow up on this and report back.

Your hypothesis that this is a network level issue seems to be correct: the test script works when setting environment variable `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1`. While this appears not be to an XLA/JAX issue, are you perhaps aware of any resources for configuring soft RoCE on linux? There seems to be very little out there other than an [NVIDIA document](https://enterprise-support.nvidia.com/s/article/howto-configure-soft-roce) that describes using the now-deprecated (apparently) `rxe_cfg` utility.
I dont think we have many soft RoCE customers, so my experience on this is a bit insufficient to comment on this. Maybe ask on nccl's forum or NVIDIA network support?
Closing this since it doesn't look like a JAX issue? Feel free to reopen if I am wrong :)

### Description

I'm experiencing difficulty in getting a simple `jax.distributed` test working properly. The test script for the coordinator, `host0`, is
```python
import jax

jax.distributed.initialize(coordinator_address="host0:30000", num_processes=2, process_id=0)
print(jax.device_count())
print(jax.local_device_count())

xs = jax.numpy.ones(jax.local_device_count())
print(jax.pmap(lambda x: jax.lax.psum(x, 'i'), axis_name='i')(xs))
```
and the script on `host1` is
```python
import jax

jax.distributed.initialize(coordinator_address="host0:30000", num_processes=2, process_id=1)
print(jax.device_count())
print(jax.local_device_count())
```

When running the scripts on their respective hosts there appears to be some initial communication as they both print correct device count and local device count values, but then `host0` prints the error

It fails with the same errors.

It looks like your network is not configured properly based on this warning:
`misc/ibvwrap.cc:206 NCCL WARN Call to ibv_modify_qp failed with error Invalid argument errno 22`
Your cross-node comm interface is using RoCE:
`host1:20632:21039 [3] NCCL INFO NET/IB : Using [0]irdma0:1/RoCE [RO]; `

This usually happens when the NIC is not configured properly to use RoCE.
Here is some debugging info provided by NCCL:
https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html#rdma-over-converged-ethernet-roce

Can you also use this perftest(https://github.com/linux-rdma/perftest) tool to see if your network is RoCE enabled?
Thanks, I'll follow up on this and report back.

Your hypothesis that this is a network level issue seems to be correct: the test script works when setting environment variable `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1`. While this appears not be to an XLA/JAX issue, are you perhaps aware of any resources for configuring soft RoCE on linux? There seems to be very little out there other than an [NVIDIA document](https://enterprise-support.nvidia.com/s/article/howto-configure-soft-roce) that describes using the now-deprecated (apparently) `rxe_cfg` utility.
I dont think we have many soft RoCE customers, so my experience on this is a bit insufficient to comment on this. Maybe ask on nccl's forum or NVIDIA network support?
Closing this since it doesn't look like a JAX issue? Feel free to reopen if I am wrong :)
